title: Interim Horizon Credit System for Unplanned Bursts
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Define and pilot an "Interim Horizon Credit System" (IHCS) to enable predictable, auditable short-term capacity reallocations for unplanned work mid-cycle without destabilizing committed scope. Rationale: Current ad-hoc mid-cycle requests (incidents, urgent compliance, critical bug hotfixes) cause last-minute scope churn or unbalanced staffing. IHCS creates a lightweight financialized signal (credits) teams can spend to temporarily borrow capacity or request fast-track staff reassignments, governed by clear rules and telemetry.

Core mechanics:
- Credit budget: Each initiative receives a small baseline of 'Horizon Credits' at cycle start (configurable fraction of total points) plus an unallocated pool for org-level spikes. Credits are additive and can be banked up to a cap (e.g., 25% of baseline).
- Earning: Teams may earn additional credits via delivery performance (ahead-of-commit velocity bonus), cross-team lending, or leadership discretionary allotments for strategic opportunities.
- Spending: To spend credits, a team files a 'credit spend request' in the Cycle Planner UI including: impact statement, rollback plan, estimated points, and a minimum approval path. Very small spends (<2 credits) auto-approve; medium spends require functional lead + PM approval; large spends (>8 credits) require the Cycle Steward committee sign-off.
- Scoring: Requests are scored by urgency, customer impact, rollback complexity, and dependency footprint. A simple 0-10 score drives auto-approve/hold/escalate thresholds.
- Timebox & expiry: Credits used for bursts are timeboxed (2–6 weeks depending on request size) and expire at cycle end unless explicitly extended by committee.
- Accountability: Every spend creates an IO entry with expected outcomes and a mandatory rollback criterion. Teams that overspend without acceptable outcomes are penalized with reduced future baseline credits (governance lever).

Acceptance criteria:
- Design doc and UI mockups published in Confluence (link below).
- Pilot: 3 volunteer teams complete at least one credit spend flow and report results.
- Telemetry: Redwood Console dashboard shows credit balances, spend rate, average approval latency, and post-spend outcome (delivered/rolled-back/partial).
- Governance: Charter for a 5-person Cycle Steward committee with clear SLA (24–48h decision window for escalations).

Risk & trade-offs:
- Risk of gaming the system (teams deliberately undercommitting to earn credits) — mitigated by tying earning to forward velocity and post-spend outcome checks.
- Administrative overhead — mitigate by low-friction flows and automated approvals for small spends.
- Cultural resistance to 'financializing' capacity — emphasize this is an interim, lightweight tool to reduce unstructured interruptions and make implicit trade-offs explicit.

Implementation outline & milestones:
- Week 1: Finalize scoring rubric and committee charter.
- Week 2: Confluence doc + Console pilot UI prototype (read-only) for visibility.
- Week 3: Build credit API (read/write), simple Cycle Planner form, and approval workflow.
- Week 4–8: Pilot with 3 teams, collect telemetry and retrospective.
- Post-pilot: Iterate on thresholds, consider integrating with Cycle capacity simulator.

Dependencies: console-ux team (approval UI), infra team (credits API and RBAC), cycle-planner data (velocity & committed points), legal for any policy language.

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/IHCS-draft
- Console mock (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/IHCS-mockups
- Cycle Planner proposal doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1IHCS-prop

Metrics to monitor: "credit_spend_rate", "approval_latency_hours", "post_spend_success_pct", "unplanned_scope_delta_points", "team_credit_balance_variance".

Rollout decision criteria: Proceed to broader rollout if pilot shows: average approval latency <48h, post_spend_success_pct >= 75%, and no gaming detected in audit sample.
